question: MADR 0043 reversal trigger 3 asks whether Infinigen Indoors can be 'driven by environmentId / case blueprint fields'. The concrete, untested sub-question: can it emit an empty shell whose footprint, height and door placement are SPECIFIED as inputs?

source.installPatch: infinigen/terrain/__init__.py restored to pre-2024-08-28 upstream state ('from .core import Terrain, hidden_in_viewport'); upstream emptied it for a circular-import fix that does not trigger on the generate_indoors entry path (generate_indoors.py:48 imports Terrain).

venv.installMethod: python3.11 -m venv + INFINIGEN_MINIMAL_INSTALL=True INFINIGEN_INSTALL_TERRAIN=False pip install -e . (same recipe as the prior /tmp/ocxr77_tools install)

runs.ginConfig: disable/clinical_bay.gin (no_trim.gin = no_objects + doors/windows/skirting off; RoomConstants.global_params.wall_height=2.65; wall_thickness=('uniform',0.2,0.25); aspect_ratio_range=(2.0,2.1))

orchestrator summary + issue-271 worker blend measure

runs.triangleCountNote: 7,050,241 tris measured but this run used fast_solve+singleroom WITHOUT the no_trim furniture-free override, so the count is furniture-inclusive and is NOT an architecture number. Do not report it as architecture.

heightIsControllable.verdict: MET — height is a hard, exact, deterministic gin input.
evidence: RoomConstants.global_params.wall_height is @gin.configurable (infinigen/core/constraints/constraint_language/constants.py:50-56) and is consumed by the solidifier as the room shell height (infinigen/core/constraints/example_solver/room/solidifier.py:295-299) and the solver's dimension tuple (infinigen/core/constraints/example_solver/room/floor_plan.py:147-151).
wall_height=2.65 -> measured room shell height exactly 2.65 m in BOTH baseline runs (clinical_bay, clinical_bay_control) despite different footprints/seeds.
wall_height=3.6 -> measured room shell height exactly 3.6 m (dimctl_h36).
Determinism control: two runs with the same wall_height but different footprints (25.61x18.00 vs 22.00x18.52) measure identical scene height 3.851 — the height does not vary with seed/contour noise.

footprintTargeting.verdict: NOT MET as an input — absolute footprint (width x depth) cannot be specified; it is DERIVED from soft per-room-type area objectives.
evidence: infinigen/core/constraints/example_solver/room/graph.py:273-289 (suggest_dimensions): footprint = sqrt(area*aspect) x sqrt(area/aspect), where area = SUM(typical_areas[room_type]) * slackness (graph.py:276-281).
typical_areas are DERIVED by evaluating each room type against the constraint graph at sizes 1.5-25 m (graph.py:296-344) — not read from any input.

Per-room area TARGETS are hardcoded soft objectives in infinigen_examples/constraints/home.py:354-382 (e.g. (r.area()/20).log().hinge(0,0.4).pow(2) for DiningRoom; /40 for Bedroom/LivingRoom; /5 for Closet).

The only footprint SHAPE knob, RoomConstants.aspect_ratio_range (constants.py:26-27, consumed at graph.py:282-289), is damped: (0.9,1.0) -> house 22.0x18.52 (aspect 1.19); (2.0,2.1) -> house 25.61x18.00 (aspect 1.42). It moves the whole-floorplan contour, not a target bay of 7.0x3.45.

restrict_solving.restrict_parent_rooms=['DiningRoom'] does NOT collapse the room set (7 rooms emitted) — it restricts object-solving domains only (infinigen_examples/util/generate_indoors_util.py:216-221, 233-236).

doorPlacement.verdict: NOT MET as an input — door aperture POSITION is random; door WIDTH/HEIGHT are constants derived from RoomConstants (and door_params is not gin-exposed).
evidence: Door cutters are placed at a uniform random fraction along shared interior edges (infinigen/core/constraints/example_solver/room/solidifier.py:549 y = uniform(min+m, max-m)) and along the longest exterior edge for the entrance (solidifier.py:565 lam = uniform(m/len, 1-m/len)).
door_params (door_width_ratio, door_size) LACK the @gin.configurable decorator (constants.py:67-77); gin rejects 'RoomConstants.door_params.door_size' with 'No configurable matching'.
Measured door apertures: 0.898 m wide x 2.185 m tall (defaults sampled), positions random.

clinicalSemantics.verdict: NOT MEASURED THIS SLICE — the room set remains residential (balcony/bathroom/bedroom/closet/dining-room/kitchen/living-room). MADR 0043's Decision already records that there is no clinical-station vocabulary; this slice measured dimensions, not semantics.

ginParametersWithFileLine.RoomConstants.global_params.unit: constants.py:54 (default 0.5; quantizes all dimensions via unit_cast constants.py:113-116)
ginParametersWithFileLine.RoomConstants.global_params.segment_marg: constants.py:55 (default 1.4; min shared-edge length for a door, solidifier.py:442; door width base)
ginParametersWithFileLine.RoomConstants.global_params.wall_height: constants.py:56 (default ('uniform',2.8,3.2); THE ceiling-height input — proven controllable)
ginParametersWithFileLine.RoomConstants.room_type: constants.py:23,26-27 (graph vocabulary; not exercised — gin cannot parse Semantics enums into the un-annotated param)
ginParametersWithFileLine.restrict_solving.solve_max_rooms: infinigen_examples/util/generate_indoors_util.py:206,220 (documented 'only place objects in at most this many rooms')
ginParametersWithFileLine.home_room_constraints area targets: infinigen_examples/constraints/home.py:354-382 (hardcoded soft area objectives per room type)

cliUsageNote: generate_indoors.py's -p option uses nargs='+': REPEATED -p FLAGS REPLACE RATHER THAN APPEND — only the last -p value survives. All overrides must be passed under ONE -p: '-p A=1 "B=[\"x\"]" C=2'. The existing probe scripts already do this (infinigen-indoors-cagematch-probe.ts); two early attempts in this slice re-discovered it (a lone surviving override silently skipped terrain_enabled and crashed on missing terrain libs).
conclusion: Lane C cagematch, decision-with-evidence: the HEIGHT axis of reversal trigger 3 is MET and measured (wall_height is an exact, deterministic, gin-configurable input: 2.65 -> 2.65 m shell, 3.6 -> 3.6 m shell, identical scene height across differing footprints). The FOOTPRINT axis is a measured negative: absolute width x depth is not an input — it is derived from hardcoded soft area objectives (home.py:354-382 via graph.py:273-289), and the aspect knob is damped. The DOOR-PLACEMENT axis is a measured negative: positions are uniform-random (solidifier.py:549/565). MADR 0043's Decision therefore stands unchanged: Infinigen remains not adopted as an environmentId-driven runtime source; hand-made parametric shells stay. The 'parameterisable' objection from MADR 0043 is now closed on measurement rather than inference — the blocker is not room semantics but the ABSENCE of absolute dimension inputs in the solver, and the height half of parameterisation IS available.
